parts.text: Paul, Silvanus, and Timotheus greet the Thessalonian church and continually thank God for its work of faith, labour of love, and steadfast hope in Jesus Christ. They recognize God’s choosing of these beloved believers because the gospel arrived not as words alone but with power, the Holy Ghost, and deep assurance, accompanied by the missionaries’ evident conduct.

The Thessalonians received the word amid much affliction with joy from the Holy Ghost, following the Lord and his messengers. Their faith has made them examples throughout Macedonia and Achaia and become widely known beyond those regions. Others recount how they turned from idols to serve the living and true God and await his Son from heaven: the risen Jesus, who delivers from coming wrath.

chapters.title: A ministry of integrity and affection

parts.text: Paul recalls preaching boldly despite suffering at Philippi. His ministry did not depend on deception, flattery, greed, or a desire for human praise, but on pleasing God who tests hearts. The missionaries treated the believers gently, sharing their lives as well as the gospel, and worked night and day to avoid burdening them. Like a caring father, Paul urged each person toward conduct worthy of the God who calls them to his kingdom and glory.

Paul thanks God that they received the message as God’s word, which works in believers. Their suffering from their own countrymen resembles that of Judean churches, and he condemns persecutors who obstruct the Gentile mission. Though separated physically, the missionaries remain deeply attached to them. Paul has repeatedly wanted to return, but Satan hindered him. The Thessalonians are his hope, joy, and crown before Jesus at his coming.

Unable to bear uncertainty about the Thessalonians, Paul remained in Athens and sent Timotheus to strengthen and encourage their faith. They had already been warned that affliction belongs to their calling, and those trials had indeed come. Paul feared the tempter might exploit their suffering and undo the missionaries’ labour, so he sought to learn how their faith was holding.

Timotheus returns with good news of their faith, love, and desire to see Paul. Their steadfastness comforts him amid his own distress and fills him with gratitude and joy. He prays earnestly to see them and supply what their faith still lacks. Paul asks God to direct his return and cause their love for one another and everyone to increase, establishing them in blameless holiness at Jesus’ coming with all his saints.

chapters.title: Holiness and hope for departed believers

parts.text: Paul urges increasing obedience to the instructions received through Jesus. God’s will is their holiness: they must abstain from sexual immorality, live honourably rather than in uncontrolled desire, and avoid wronging others. Rejecting this instruction rejects God, who gives his Holy Spirit. Their brotherly love already reaches Macedonia, but should grow further. They should live quietly, attend to their responsibilities, and work with their hands, behaving honestly toward outsiders and providing for their needs.

Believers should not grieve over the dead as those without hope. Since Jesus died and rose, God will bring those sleeping in Jesus with him. At the Lord’s descent with a shout, the archangel’s voice, and God’s trumpet, the dead in Christ rise first. Living believers then join them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, remaining with him forever. They should comfort one another with this promise.

chapters.title: Watchful lives and a caring community

parts.text: The day of the Lord comes unexpectedly like a thief, bringing destruction when people speak of peace and safety. Believers, however, belong to the light and should live awake and sober, clothed with faith, love, and salvation’s hope. God has appointed them to salvation through Jesus rather than wrath; his death secures life together with him. They should therefore encourage and build one another up.

Paul calls for respect toward spiritual workers, peace within the church, correction of the unruly, comfort for the fainthearted, support for the weak, and patience with everyone. They must pursue good instead of revenge, continually rejoice, pray, and give thanks. They should neither quench the Spirit nor despise prophecy, but test everything and hold to what is good. Paul prays for their complete sanctification and preservation until Christ comes, asks for prayer, and directs that the letter be read to all.
